newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX oil complex seen higher in slight recovery.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX oil complex seen higher in slight recovery.

text.p: The NYMEX oil complex was called higher early Thursday, continuing Wednesday's buying spree on softer oil prices, traders said.
"It's follow-through from yesterday. There was some buying at the close at these lower levels," said a trader.

Heating oil was called 0.25 to 0.50 cent a gallon higher after losing 11 percent in the past two weeks from its post-Gulf War high of 76.75 made October 8. Crude was called 15 to 20 cents a barrel higher while gasoline was called 0.50 to 0.75 cent a gallon higher.

"Technically we were able to hold support for crude at $24.00 yesterday and that was encouraging," said Refco Energy Group vice president Victor Yu, explaining the bounce in oil prices was also due to technical buying.

Gasoline has been relatively strong due to tightening supplies. A focus on distillate output has refiners cutting back on gasoline production at a time when supplies are at 20- year lows, traders said. On Wednesday, November gasoline ended up 0.90 cent at 70.00 cents a gallon.
December crude settled off six cents a barrel at $24.28 while Nov heat ended off 1.37 cents at 68.46 cents a gallon.

In the headlines, Norway's Statoil said Thursday it had shut in oil production at the 250,000 barrels per day Heidrun field due to a technical snag. But traders said the news had no noticeable effect on oil prices in overnight ACCESS trading.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
